source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact tab-separated Greek payload, retaining whitespace and variant markers.

method: Every pinned Greek verse read before authoring. All verses drafted before reading prior Fluent. TSW is a post-authoring comparator, not a wording template. Each authored verse has its own rationale. F0–F3 choices are provisional; no independent review or change quota.

chapters.tsw_alignment_reason: Pinned 1 John 2:14 includes the children address placed at the end of TSW 2:13. Label-level comparators remain unchanged; compare 2:13–14 together.

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated what and bodily testimony without prematurely resolving the word's referent.
verses.before: What was from the beginning, what we have heard, what we have seen with our eyes, what we looked at and our hands touched, concerning the word of life—
verses.after: What was from the beginning, what we have heard, what we have seen with our own eyes, what we looked upon and our hands touched, concerning the word of life—
verses.tsw_comparator: That which was from the beginning, which we have heard, which we have seen with our eyes, which we looked upon and have touched with our hands, concerning the word of life—

verses.rationale: Keeps revealed repeated and the movement from with the Father to the witnesses.
verses.before: the life was revealed, and we have seen it and testify to it and proclaim to you the eternal life that was with the Father and was revealed to us—
verses.after: the life was revealed, and we have seen it and bear witness and announce to you the eternal life that was with the Father and was revealed to us—
verses.tsw_comparator: the life was made manifest, and we have seen it and testify to it and proclaim to you the eternal life, which was with the Father and was made manifest to us—

verses.rationale: Retains the purpose of testimony and both dimensions of fellowship.
verses.before: what we have seen and heard we also proclaim to you, so that you too may have fellowship with us. And our fellowship is with the Father and with his Son, Jesus Christ.
verses.after: what we have seen and heard we announce to you too, so that you may share in fellowship with us. And our fellowship is with the Father and with his Son, Jesus Christ.
verses.tsw_comparator: that which we have seen and heard we proclaim also to you, so that you too may have fellowship with us; and indeed our fellowship is with the Father and with his Son Jesus Christ.

verses.rationale: Follows the pinned our rather than your joy reading.
verses.before: We are writing these things so that our joy may be complete.
verses.after: We write these things so that our joy may be complete.
verses.tsw_comparator: And we are writing these things so that our joy may be complete.

verses.rationale: Preserves light as a direct metaphor and the emphatic absence of darkness.
verses.before: This is the message we have heard from him and proclaim to you: God is light, and in him there is no darkness at all.
verses.after: This is the message we have heard from him and announce to you: God is light, and there is no darkness in him at all.
verses.tsw_comparator: This is the message we have heard from him and proclaim to you, that God is light, and in him there is no darkness at all.

verses.rationale: Keeps the inclusive we, walking image and truth as enacted.
verses.before: If we say that we have fellowship with him while we walk in darkness, we lie and do not practice the truth.
verses.after: If we say we have fellowship with him while walking in darkness, we lie and do not practice the truth.
verses.tsw_comparator: If we say that we have fellowship with him while we walk in darkness, we lie and do not practice the truth.

verses.rationale: Preserves mutual fellowship and bodily cleansing language without adding Christ to Jesus.
verses.before: But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship with one another, and the blood of Jesus his Son cleanses us from all sin.
verses.after: But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship with one another, and the blood of Jesus his Son cleanses us from every sin.
verses.tsw_comparator: But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship with one another, and the blood of Jesus his Son cleanses us from all sin.

verses.rationale: Retains the self-directed consequence and recurring conditional form.
verses.before: If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us.
verses.after: If we say we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us.
verses.tsw_comparator: If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us.

verses.rationale: Preserves faithful/righteous and forgiveness/cleansing pairs with recurring righteousness vocabulary.
verses.before: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive our sins and cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
verses.after: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and righteous to forgive our sins and cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
verses.tsw_comparator: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.

verses.rationale: Keeps the distinction between no sin and not having sinned and the accusation's force.
verses.before: If we say that we have not sinned, we make him a liar, and his word is not in us.
verses.after: If we say we have not sinned, we make him a liar, and his word is not in us.
verses.tsw_comparator: If we say that we have not sinned, we make him a liar, and his word is not in us.

verses.rationale: Keeps affectionate address, purpose and provision without weakening either statement.
verses.before: My little children, I am writing these things to you so that you may not sin. But if anyone does sin, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous.
verses.after: My little children, I write these things to you so that you will not sin. But if anyone sins, we have an advocate with the Father: Jesus Christ, the righteous one.
verses.tsw_comparator: My little children, I am writing these things to you so that you may not sin. But if anyone does sin, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous.

verses.rationale: Retains the atonement term with an explanatory range in notes and the worldwide scope.
verses.before: He is the atoning sacrifice for our sins, and not for ours only but also for the whole world.
verses.after: He himself is the atoning sacrifice for our sins, and not only for ours but also for the whole world's.
verses.tsw_comparator: He is the atoning sacrifice for our sins, and not for ours only but also for the whole world.

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated knowing and the practical criterion rather than making knowledge merely cognitive.
verses.before: By this we know that we have come to know him: if we keep his commandments.
verses.after: This is how we know that we have come to know him: we keep his commands.
verses.tsw_comparator: And by this we know that we have come to know him, if we keep his commandments.

verses.rationale: Retains the direct claim, contrary conduct and blunt judgment.
verses.before: Whoever says, “I know him,” but does not keep his commandments is a liar, and the truth is not in that person.
verses.after: Anyone who says, “I know him,” but does not keep his commands is a liar, and the truth is not in that person.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever says “I know him” but does not keep his commandments is a liar, and the truth is not in him,

verses.rationale: Keeps the love-of-God phrase open and links the next verse as the criterion.
verses.before: But whoever keeps his word, in that person the love of God has truly been brought to completion. By this we know that we are in him:
verses.after: But in anyone who keeps his word, the love of God has truly reached its fullness. This is how we know that we are in him:
verses.tsw_comparator: but whoever keeps his word, in him truly the love of God is perfected. By this we know that we are in him:

verses.rationale: Preserves remain and walk as recurring relational and behavioral images.
verses.before: whoever says they remain in him ought to walk just as he walked.
verses.after: whoever says they remain in him must also walk as he walked.
verses.tsw_comparator: whoever says he abides in him ought to walk in the same way in which he walked.

verses.rationale: Keeps the old/new tension and the shorter source without adding from the beginning twice.
verses.before: Beloved, I am not writing you a new commandment, but an old commandment that you had from the beginning. The old commandment is the word you heard.
verses.after: Beloved, I am not writing you a new command, but an old command you have had from the beginning. The old command is the word you heard.
verses.tsw_comparator: Beloved, I am writing you no new commandment, but an old commandment that you had from the beginning. The old commandment is the word that you have heard.

verses.rationale: Retains the deliberate reversal and the already of dawning light.
verses.before: Yet I am writing you a new commandment, which is true in him and in you, because the darkness is passing away and the true light is already shining.
verses.after: Yet I am writing you a new command, which is true in him and in you, because the darkness is passing away and the true light already shines.
verses.tsw_comparator: At the same time, it is a new commandment that I am writing to you, which is true in him and in you, because the darkness is passing away and the true light is already shining.

verses.rationale: Uses inclusive family language for the community while retaining the strong hate/light contrast.
verses.before: Whoever says they are in the light and hates a brother or sister is still in darkness.
verses.after: Anyone who says they are in the light but hates a brother or sister is still in darkness.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever says he is in the light and hates his brother is still in darkness.

verses.rationale: Keeps stumbling language with its ambiguity rather than adding a specific victim.
verses.before: Whoever loves a brother or sister remains in the light, and there is no cause for stumbling in that person.
verses.after: Whoever loves a brother or sister remains in the light, and there is no cause for stumbling in that person.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever loves his brother abides in the light, and in him there is no cause for stumbling.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated darkness and the movement from walking to blindness.
verses.before: But whoever hates a brother or sister is in the darkness and walks in the darkness and does not know where they are going, because the darkness has blinded their eyes.
verses.after: But whoever hates a brother or sister is in darkness and walks in darkness, not knowing where they are going because the darkness has blinded their eyes.
verses.tsw_comparator: But whoever hates his brother is in the darkness and walks in the darkness, and does not know where he is going, because the darkness has blinded his eyes.

verses.rationale: Keeps direct address and the stated ground of forgiveness.
verses.before: I am writing to you, little children, because your sins have been forgiven for his name's sake.
verses.after: I write to you, little children, because your sins have been forgiven on account of his name.
verses.tsw_comparator: I am writing to you, little children, because your sins are forgiven for his name’s sake.

verses.rationale: Retains the specifically named groups and two balanced addresses at the pinned verse boundary.
verses.before: I am writing to you, fathers, because you know the one who is from the beginning. I am writing to you, young men, because you have overcome the evil one. I have written to you, children, because you know the Father.
verses.after: I write to you, fathers, because you have known the one who is from the beginning. I write to you, young men, because you have overcome the evil one.
verses.tsw_comparator: I am writing to you, fathers, because you know him who is from the beginning. I am writing to you, young men, because you have overcome the evil one. I write to you, children, because you know the Father.

verses.rationale: Preserves the tense shift and all three addresses in the source's verse 14.
verses.before: I have written to you, fathers, because you know the one who is from the beginning. I have written to you, young men, because you are strong, and the word of God remains in you, and you have overcome the evil one.
verses.after: I have written to you, children, because you have known the Father. I have written to you, fathers, because you have known the one who is from the beginning. I have written to you, young men, because you are strong, God's word remains in you, and you have overcome the evil one.
verses.tsw_comparator: I write to you, fathers, because you know him who is from the beginning. I write to you, young men, because you are strong, and the word of God abides in you, and you have overcome the evil one.

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated world and leaves the genitive love of the Father open.
verses.before: Do not love the world or the things in the world. If anyone loves the world, the love of the Father is not in that person.
verses.after: Do not love the world or the things in the world. If anyone loves the world, the love of the Father is not in that person.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not love the world or the things in the world. If anyone loves the world, the love of the Father is not in him.

verses.rationale: Retains both desires and the worldly-life term, explained in the note.
verses.before: For everything in the world—the desire of the flesh, the desire of the eyes, and the pride of life—is not from the Father but from the world.
verses.after: For everything in the world—the desire of the flesh, the desire of the eyes and pride in one's possessions—is from the world, not from the Father.
verses.tsw_comparator: For all that is in the world—the desire of the flesh and the desire of the eyes and the pride of life—is not from the Father but is from the world.

verses.rationale: Keeps the contrast in passing and remaining without moralizing beyond the text.
verses.before: The world is passing away, along with its desire, but whoever does the will of God remains forever.
verses.after: The world and its desire are passing away, but whoever does God's will remains forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the world is passing away along with its desire, but whoever does the will of God abides forever.

verses.rationale: Retains singular and plural antichrist and repeated time claim without assigning a modern identity.
verses.before: Children, it is the last hour. As you have heard that antichrist is coming, even now many antichrists have come. From this we know that it is the last hour.
verses.after: Children, it is the last hour. You heard that antichrist is coming, and now many antichrists have appeared. That is how we know it is the last hour.
verses.tsw_comparator: Children, it is the last hour, and as you have heard that antichrist is coming, so now many antichrists have come. Therefore we know that it is the last hour.

verses.rationale: Unpacks the departure clause while documenting the scope of the final all/not expression.
verses.before: They went out from us, but they were not of us. For if they had been of us, they would have remained with us. But they went out so that it might become clear that none of them are of us.
verses.after: They went out from us, but they did not belong to us. If they had belonged to us, they would have remained with us. Their departure made clear that none of them belonged to us.
verses.tsw_comparator: They went out from us, but they were not of us; for if they had been of us, they would have remained with us. But they went out, that it might become plain that they all are not of us.

verses.rationale: Follows the pinned all of you rather than all things and leaves the Holy One unnamed.
verses.before: But you have an anointing from the Holy One, and all of you know.
verses.after: But you have an anointing from the Holy One, and all of you know.
verses.tsw_comparator: But you have been anointed by the Holy One, and you all have knowledge.

verses.rationale: Preserves the negative/positive reason and the source's contrast of truth and lie.
verses.before: I am writing to you not because you do not know the truth, but because you know it and because no lie comes from the truth.
verses.after: I have written to you because you know the truth, not because you do not know it, and because no lie comes from the truth.
verses.tsw_comparator: I write to you, not because you do not know the truth, but because you know it, and because no lie is of the truth.

verses.rationale: Keeps the confession-specific referent and both divine relational names.
verses.before: Who is the liar but the one who denies that Jesus is the Christ? This is the antichrist: the one who denies the Father and the Son.
verses.after: Who is the liar but the one who denies that Jesus is the Christ? This is the antichrist: the one who denies the Father and the Son.
verses.tsw_comparator: Who is the liar but the one who denies that Jesus is the Christ? This is the antichrist, the one who denies the Father and the Son.

verses.rationale: Preserves both halves of the contrast and the positive confession clause.
verses.before: No one who denies the Son has the Father. Whoever confesses the Son has the Father also.
verses.after: Everyone who denies the Son is without the Father as well. Whoever acknowledges the Son has the Father too.
verses.tsw_comparator: No one who denies the Son has the Father. Whoever confesses the Son has the Father also.

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated remaining and the conditional relation.
verses.before: Let what you heard from the beginning remain in you. If what you heard from the beginning remains in you, then you also will remain in the Son and in the Father.
verses.after: As for you, let what you heard from the beginning remain in you. If it remains in you, you too will remain in the Son and in the Father.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let what you heard from the beginning abide in you. If what you heard from the beginning abides in you, then you too will abide in the Son and in the Father.

verses.rationale: Preserves emphatic promise and its named content.
verses.before: And this is the promise he made to us: eternal life.
verses.after: And this is the promise he himself made to us: eternal life.
verses.tsw_comparator: And this is the promise that he made to us—eternal life.

verses.rationale: Makes the active misleading force clear without inventing identities.
verses.before: I am writing these things to you about those who are trying to deceive you.
verses.after: I have written these things about those who are trying to lead you astray.
verses.tsw_comparator: I write these things to you about those who are trying to deceive you.

verses.rationale: Keeps the difficult no-teacher claim and repeated anointing without resolving its scope by added explanation.
verses.before: But the anointing you received from him remains in you, and you do not need anyone to teach you. Rather, as his anointing teaches you about all things and is true and is not a lie, just as it taught you, remain in him.
verses.after: As for you, the anointing you received from him remains in you, and you do not need anyone to teach you. His anointing teaches you about all things; it is true and is no lie. So remain in him, just as it taught you.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the anointing that you received from him abides in you, and you have no need that anyone should teach you. But as his anointing teaches you about all things, and is true and is not a lie—just as it has taught you, abide in him.

verses.rationale: Retains revealed/coming and the contrast of confidence and shame.
verses.before: And now, little children, remain in him, so that when he appears we may have confidence and not shrink from him in shame at his coming.
verses.after: And now, little children, remain in him, so that when he is revealed we may have confidence and not shrink from him in shame at his coming.
verses.tsw_comparator: And now, little children, abide in him, so that when he appears we may have confidence and not shrink from him in shame at his coming.

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated knowing, righteousness and divine birth without assigning an unnecessary pronoun referent.
verses.before: If you know that he is righteous, you know that everyone who practices righteousness has been born of him.
verses.after: If you know that he is righteous, you know that everyone who practices righteousness has been born of him.
verses.tsw_comparator: If you know that he is righteous, you may be sure that everyone who practices righteousness has been born of him.

verses.rationale: Retains the source's and we are and the parallel failures to know.
verses.before: See what kind of love the Father has given us, that we should be called children of God—and we are. This is why the world does not know us: it did not know him.
verses.after: See what love the Father has given us, that we should be called God's children—and that is what we are! The world does not know us because it did not know him.
verses.tsw_comparator: See what kind of love the Father has given us, that we should be called children of God—and we are. Because of this, the world does not know us, because it did not know him.

verses.rationale: Keeps present identity and future uncertainty; the note preserves the alternative when it is revealed.
verses.before: Beloved, we are God's children now, and what we will be has not yet been revealed. We know that when he is revealed, we will be like him, because we will see him as he is.
verses.after: Beloved, we are God's children now, and what we will be has not yet been revealed. We know that when he is revealed, we will be like him, because we will see him as he is.
verses.tsw_comparator: Beloved, we are God’s children now, and what we will be has not yet been revealed. We know that when he is revealed, we will be like him, because we will see him as he is.

verses.rationale: Preserves the hope's object and the comparison without identifying a new referent.
verses.before: Everyone who has this hope in him purifies themselves, just as he is pure.
verses.after: Everyone who has this hope in him purifies themselves, just as he is pure.
verses.tsw_comparator: And everyone who has this hope in him purifies themselves, just as he is pure.

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated terms and direct definition.
verses.before: Everyone who practices sin also practices lawlessness; sin is lawlessness.
verses.after: Everyone who commits sin also commits lawlessness. Sin is lawlessness.
verses.tsw_comparator: Everyone who practices sin also practices lawlessness, and sin is lawlessness.

verses.rationale: Follows the source's sins without an added our and retains the sinless claim.
verses.before: You know that he was revealed to take away sins, and in him there is no sin.
verses.after: You know that he was revealed to take away sins, and there is no sin in him.
verses.tsw_comparator: And you know that he was revealed to take away sins, and in him there is no sin.

verses.rationale: Preserves the categorical statements and their tension with 1:8–2:2 rather than silently softening them.
verses.before: Everyone who remains in him does not sin; everyone who sins has neither seen him nor known him.
verses.after: No one who remains in him sins. No one who sins has seen him or known him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Everyone who remains in him does not sin; everyone who sins has neither seen him nor known him.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated righteousness and the comparison.
verses.before: Little children, let no one deceive you. Whoever practices righteousness is righteous, just as he is righteous.
verses.after: Little children, do not let anyone lead you astray. Whoever practices righteousness is righteous, just as he is righteous.
verses.tsw_comparator: Little children, let no one deceive you. Whoever practices righteousness is righteous, just as he is righteous.

verses.rationale: Keeps the source's strong attribution, temporal claim and stated purpose.
verses.before: Whoever practices sin is of the devil, because the devil has sinned from the beginning. The Son of God was revealed for this purpose: to destroy the works of the devil.
verses.after: Whoever commits sin is of the devil, because the devil has been sinning from the beginning. The Son of God was revealed for this purpose: to destroy the devil's works.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever practices sin is of the devil, because the devil has sinned from the beginning. The Son of God was revealed for this purpose: to destroy the works of the devil.

verses.rationale: Retains the absolute wording and unexplained seed metaphor instead of adding a habitual-sin qualification.
verses.before: Everyone who has been born of God does not practice sin, because God's seed remains in them; and they are not able to sin, because they have been born of God.
verses.after: No one born of God commits sin, because God's seed remains in them. They cannot sin, because they have been born of God.
verses.tsw_comparator: Everyone who has been born of God does not practice sin, because God’s seed remains in them; and they are not able to sin, because they have been born of God.

verses.rationale: Preserves the two families and paired criteria, using inclusive language for community kinship.
verses.before: By this the children of God and the children of the devil are evident: whoever does not practice righteousness is not of God, nor is the one who does not love a brother or sister.
verses.after: This is how God's children and the devil's children are made clear: anyone who does not practice righteousness is not of God, nor is anyone who does not love a brother or sister.
verses.tsw_comparator: By this the children of God and the children of the devil are evident: everyone who does not practice righteousness is not of God, nor is the one who does not love a brother or sister.

verses.rationale: Keeps the recurring beginning and reciprocal command.
verses.before: This is the message you heard from the beginning: that we should love one another.
verses.after: This is the message you have heard from the beginning: we should love one another.
verses.tsw_comparator: For this is the message that you heard from the beginning: that we should love one another.

verses.rationale: Retains the violent verb, male sibling and explicit question and answer.
verses.before: We should not be like Cain, who was of the evil one and killed his brother. And why did he kill him? Because his own deeds were evil, while his brother's were righteous.
verses.after: We must not be like Cain, who was of the evil one and slaughtered his brother. And why did he slaughter him? Because his own deeds were evil and his brother's were righteous.
verses.tsw_comparator: We should not be like Cain, who was of the evil one and killed his brother. And why did he kill him? Because his own deeds were evil, but his brother’s were righteous.

verses.rationale: Preserves conditional hatred without making a wider claim about outsiders.
verses.before: Do not be surprised, brothers and sisters, if the world hates you.
verses.after: Do not be surprised, brothers and sisters, if the world hates you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not be surprised, brothers and sisters, if the world hates you.

verses.rationale: Keeps passage and remaining images and the shorter second clause without an added object.
verses.before: We know that we have passed from death into life because we love our brothers and sisters. Whoever does not love remains in death.
verses.after: We know that we have passed from death to life because we love our brothers and sisters. Anyone who does not love remains in death.
verses.tsw_comparator: We know that we have passed from death into life because we love the brothers and sisters. Whoever does not love remains in death.

verses.rationale: Retains the forceful equation and recurring remain language.
verses.before: Everyone who hates a brother or sister is a murderer, and you know that no murderer has eternal life remaining in them.
verses.after: Everyone who hates a brother or sister is a murderer, and you know that no murderer has eternal life remaining in them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Everyone who hates a brother or sister is a murderer, and you know that no murderer has eternal life remaining in them.

verses.rationale: Preserves the singular example and plural obligation with the same life language.
verses.before: By this we have come to know love: he laid down his life for us, and we ought to lay down our lives for our brothers and sisters.
verses.after: This is how we have come to know love: he laid down his life for us. We too ought to lay down our lives for our brothers and sisters.
verses.tsw_comparator: By this we have known love: he laid down his life for us, and we ought to lay down our lives for the brothers and sisters.

verses.rationale: Renders the bodily compassion idiom naturally while retaining the rhetorical question and open love-of-God phrase.
verses.before: But if anyone has the world's goods and sees a brother or sister in need and closes their heart against them, how can the love of God remain in that person?
verses.after: If someone has this world's goods, sees a brother or sister in need and shuts off compassion for them, how can the love of God remain in that person?
verses.tsw_comparator: But whoever has the goods of the world and sees a brother or sister in need and closes their heart against them, how can the love of God remain in that person?

verses.rationale: Preserves the word/deed and speech/truth contrasts; alone expresses the contrast without denying spoken love.
verses.before: Little children, let us not love in word or speech, but in deed and truth.
verses.after: Little children, let us love in deed and truth, not in word or speech alone.
verses.tsw_comparator: Little children, let us not love in word or speech, but in deed and truth.

verses.rationale: Keeps the prospective knowing and heart language, carrying the reason into the next verse.
verses.before: By this we will know that we are of the truth and will reassure our hearts before him,
verses.after: This is how we will know that we are of the truth and reassure our hearts before him:
verses.tsw_comparator: By this we will know that we are of the truth, and we will reassure our hearts before him,

verses.rationale: Retains the greater-than and all-knowing claims without spelling out a theological resolution of condemnation.
verses.before: whenever our heart condemns us, because God is greater than our heart and knows all things.
verses.after: whenever our hearts condemn us, God is greater than our hearts and knows everything.
verses.tsw_comparator: whenever our heart condemns us, because God is greater than our heart and knows all things.

verses.rationale: Preserves the conditional confidence and the sentence's link to the next verse.
verses.before: Beloved, if our heart does not condemn us, we have confidence before God,
verses.after: Beloved, if our hearts do not condemn us, we have confidence before God,
verses.tsw_comparator: Beloved, if our heart does not condemn us, we have confidence before God,

verses.rationale: Keeps the broad request language and the given reasons without promising specific outcomes beyond the passage.
verses.before: and whatever we ask we receive from him, because we keep his commandments and do what is pleasing before him.
verses.after: and we receive from him whatever we ask, because we keep his commands and do what pleases him.
verses.tsw_comparator: and whatever we ask we receive from him, because we keep his commandments and do what is pleasing before him.

verses.rationale: Preserves singular command with two coordinated obligations and the name language.
verses.before: And this is his commandment: that we trust in the name of his Son Jesus Christ and love one another, just as he commanded us.
verses.after: And this is his command: that we believe in the name of his Son, Jesus Christ, and love one another, just as he commanded us.
verses.tsw_comparator: And this is his commandment: that we trust in the name of his Son Jesus Christ and love one another, just as he gave us a commandment.

verses.rationale: Keeps reciprocal remaining and the Spirit as the stated basis of knowledge.
verses.before: The one who keeps his commandments remains in him, and he in them. By this we know that he remains in us: by the Spirit whom he gave us.
verses.after: Whoever keeps his commands remains in him, and he in them. This is how we know that he remains in us: by the Spirit he has given us.
verses.tsw_comparator: The one who keeps his commandments remains in him, and he in them. And by this we know that he remains in us: by the Spirit whom he gave us.

verses.rationale: Preserves the distinction between testing spirits and the false prophets' activity.
verses.before: Beloved, do not trust every spirit, but test the spirits to see whether they are from God, because many false prophets have gone out into the world.
verses.after: Beloved, do not believe every spirit. Test the spirits to see whether they are of God, because many false prophets have gone out into the world.
verses.tsw_comparator: Beloved, do not trust every spirit, but test the spirits to see whether they are from God, because many false prophets have gone out into the world.

verses.rationale: Keeps the embodied confession and the sentence's contrast with verse 3.
verses.before: By this you know the Spirit of God: every spirit that confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is from God,
verses.after: This is how you recognize the Spirit of God: every spirit that confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is of God,
verses.tsw_comparator: By this you know the Spirit of God: every spirit that confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is from God,

verses.rationale: Follows the shorter pinned reading without repeating in the flesh; retains already and the antichrist reference.
verses.before: and every spirit that does not confess Jesus is not from God. This is the spirit of the antichrist, which you heard is coming and now is already in the world.
verses.after: and every spirit that does not confess Jesus is not of God. This is the spirit of the antichrist, which you heard was coming and is already in the world.
verses.tsw_comparator: and every spirit that does not confess Jesus is not from God. This is the spirit of the antichrist, which you heard is coming, and now is already in the world.

verses.rationale: Retains the pronouns and comparison without adding names to either one.
verses.before: Little children, you are from God and have overcome them, because the one who is in you is greater than the one who is in the world.
verses.after: You are of God, little children, and you have overcome them, because the one in you is greater than the one in the world.
verses.tsw_comparator: Little children, you are from God and have overcome them, because the one who is in you is greater than the one who is in the world.

verses.rationale: Keeps the threefold world repetition and causal relation.
verses.before: They are from the world; therefore they speak from the world's perspective, and the world listens to them.
verses.after: They are of the world. That is why they speak from the world, and the world listens to them.
verses.tsw_comparator: They are from the world; therefore they speak from the world, and the world listens to them.

verses.rationale: Preserves the speakers' specific we/us authority claim without extending it to later institutions.
verses.before: We are from God. Whoever knows God listens to us; whoever is not from God does not listen to us. By this we know the Spirit of truth and the spirit of error.
verses.after: We are of God. Whoever knows God listens to us; whoever is not of God does not listen to us. This is how we recognize the Spirit of truth and the spirit of error.
verses.tsw_comparator: We are from God. Whoever knows God listens to us; whoever is not from God does not listen to us. By this we know the Spirit of truth and the spirit of error.

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated God, divine birth and knowing as linked claims.
verses.before: Beloved, let us love one another, because love is from God. Everyone who loves has been born of God and knows God.
verses.after: Beloved, let us love one another, because love is from God. Everyone who loves has been born of God and knows God.
verses.tsw_comparator: Beloved, let us love one another, because love is from God, and everyone who loves has been born of God and knows God.

verses.rationale: Retains the direct identity statement and negative criterion.
verses.before: Whoever does not love does not know God, because God is love.
verses.after: Whoever does not love has not known God, because God is love.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever does not love does not know God, because God is love.

verses.rationale: Renders monogenēs as only with its unique-son range noted and preserves the purpose clause.
verses.before: By this God's love was revealed among us: God sent his one and only Son into the world so that we might live through him.
verses.after: This is how God's love was revealed among us: God sent his only Son into the world so that we might live through him.
verses.tsw_comparator: By this the love of God was revealed among us: God sent the only Son into the world so that we might live through him.

verses.rationale: Keeps the reversal of initiative and uses the same atonement term as 2:2.
verses.before: This is love: not that we loved God, but that he loved us and sent his Son as an atoning sacrifice for our sins.
verses.after: Love is in this: not that we loved God, but that he loved us and sent his Son as the atoning sacrifice for our sins.
verses.tsw_comparator: In this is love: not that we loved God, but that God loved us and sent the Son as an atoning sacrifice for our sins.

verses.rationale: Preserves the conditional argument and reciprocal obligation.
verses.before: Beloved, if God loved us in this way, we also ought to love one another.
verses.after: Beloved, if God loved us in this way, we too ought to love one another.
verses.tsw_comparator: Beloved, if God loved us in this way, we also ought to love one another.

verses.rationale: Keeps unseen God, mutual love and remaining without explaining whose love beyond his.
verses.before: No one has ever seen God. If we love one another, God remains in us, and his love has been brought to completion in us.
verses.after: No one has ever seen God. If we love one another, God remains in us, and his love reaches its fullness in us.
verses.tsw_comparator: No one has ever seen God. If we love one another, God remains in us, and God’s love is perfected in us.

verses.rationale: Preserves reciprocal remaining and the source's of his Spirit phrasing.
verses.before: By this we know that we remain in him and he in us: he has given us from his Spirit.
verses.after: This is how we know that we remain in him and he in us: he has given us of his Spirit.
verses.tsw_comparator: By this we know that we remain in God and God in us: because God has given us from the Spirit.

verses.rationale: Retains witness and the worldwide scope of Savior.
verses.before: We have seen and testify that the Father has sent the Son as Savior of the world.
verses.after: We have seen and bear witness that the Father sent the Son as Savior of the world.
verses.tsw_comparator: And we have seen and testify that the Father has sent the Son as Savior of the world.

verses.rationale: Keeps the confession and reciprocal indwelling in natural singular language.
verses.before: Whoever confesses that Jesus is the Son of God, God remains in them, and they in God.
verses.after: Whoever confesses that Jesus is the Son of God, God remains in that person, and that person in God.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever confesses that Jesus is the Son of God, God remains in them, and they in God.

verses.rationale: Retains knowing and believing and the repeated remain pattern.
verses.before: And we have come to know and trust the love that God has for us. God is love, and the one who remains in love remains in God, and God remains in them.
verses.after: We have come to know and believe the love God has for us. God is love, and whoever remains in love remains in God, and God remains in them.
verses.tsw_comparator: And we have come to know and trust the love that God has for us. God is love, and the one who remains in love remains in God, and God remains in them.

verses.rationale: Keeps the comparison open rather than adding a particular likeness and retains judgment.
verses.before: By this love has been brought to completion among us, so that we may have confidence on the day of judgment, because as he is, so also are we in this world.
verses.after: This is how love reaches its fullness with us, so that we may have confidence on the day of judgment: as he is, so are we in this world.
verses.tsw_comparator: By this love has been perfected with us, so that we may have confidence on the day of judgment, because as he is, so also are we in this world.

verses.rationale: Preserves the passage's love, fear and punishment argument without recasting it as a general psychological claim.
verses.before: There is no fear in love, but complete love drives out fear, because fear involves punishment. The one who fears has not been brought to completion in love.
verses.after: There is no fear in love. Complete love drives out fear, because fear involves punishment. Whoever fears has not reached fullness in love.
verses.tsw_comparator: There is no fear in love, but perfect love casts out fear, because fear carries punishment, and the one who fears has not been perfected in love.

verses.rationale: Follows the pinned text without adding him as the object of our love.
verses.before: We love because he first loved us.
verses.after: We love because he first loved us.
verses.tsw_comparator: We love because God first loved us.

verses.rationale: Keeps the blunt accusation and seen/unseen argument with inclusive community kinship.
verses.before: If someone says, “I love God,” and hates a brother or sister, that person is a liar. For the one who does not love a brother or sister whom they have seen cannot love God whom they have not seen.
verses.after: If someone says, “I love God,” but hates a brother or sister, that person is a liar. For whoever does not love a brother or sister they have seen cannot love God, whom they have not seen.
verses.tsw_comparator: If someone says, “I love God,” and hates a brother or sister, that person is a liar; for the one who does not love a brother or sister whom they have seen cannot love God whom they have not seen.

verses.rationale: Preserves the linked obligations without adding exceptions.
verses.before: And we have this commandment from him: whoever loves God must also love a brother or sister.
verses.after: This is the command we have from him: whoever loves God must also love a brother or sister.
verses.tsw_comparator: And this commandment we have from God: whoever loves God must also love a brother or sister.

verses.rationale: Keeps the birth-based analogy, with literal begetter language explained in the note.
verses.before: Everyone who trusts that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God, and everyone who loves the one who gives birth also loves the one who has been born from him.
verses.after: Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God, and everyone who loves the father loves the child born of him too.
verses.tsw_comparator: Everyone who trusts that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God, and everyone who loves the one who gives birth also loves the one who has been born from God.

verses.rationale: Retains the direction of the argument and the paired actions.
verses.before: By this we know that we love the children of God: when we love God and carry out his commandments.
verses.after: This is how we know that we love God's children: we love God and carry out his commands.
verses.tsw_comparator: By this we know that we love the children of God: when we love God and carry out God’s commandments.

verses.rationale: Keeps the open love-of-God phrase and carries the explanatory sentence forward.
verses.before: For this is the love of God: that we keep his commandments. And his commandments are not burdensome,
verses.after: For this is the love of God: that we keep his commands. And his commands are not burdensome,
verses.tsw_comparator: For this is the love of God: that we keep God’s commandments. And the commandments are not burdensome,

verses.rationale: Preserves the source's neuter everything and victory/overcome repetition.
verses.before: because everyone who has been born of God overcomes the world. And this is the victory that has overcome the world: our trust.
verses.after: because everything born of God overcomes the world. And this is the victory that has overcome the world: our faith.
verses.tsw_comparator: because everything that has been born of God overcomes the world. And this is the victory that has overcome the world—our trust.

verses.rationale: Keeps the rhetorical question and precise confession.
verses.before: Who is the one who overcomes the world except the one who trusts that Jesus is the Son of God?
verses.after: Who overcomes the world but the one who believes that Jesus is the Son of God?
verses.tsw_comparator: Who is the one who overcomes the world except the one who trusts that Jesus is the Son of God?

verses.rationale: Preserves water and blood without assigning sacramental or biographical interpretations in the text.
verses.before: This is the one who came through water and blood, Jesus Christ—not by the water only, but by the water and by the blood. And the Spirit is the one who testifies, because the Spirit is the truth.
verses.after: This is the one who came through water and blood: Jesus Christ. He came not by water alone, but by water and blood. And the Spirit bears witness, because the Spirit is the truth.
verses.tsw_comparator: This is the one who came through water and blood, Jesus Christ—not in the water only, but in the water and in the blood. And the Spirit is the one who testifies, because the Spirit is the truth.

verses.rationale: Follows the pinned short text and excludes the later heavenly-witness expansion.
verses.before: For there are three that testify:
verses.after: For there are three who bear witness:
verses.tsw_comparator: For there are three that testify:

verses.rationale: Keeps all three witnesses and renders their being toward one as agreement.
verses.before: the Spirit, the water, and the blood, and the three agree as one.
verses.after: the Spirit, the water and the blood, and the three agree.
verses.tsw_comparator: the Spirit and the water and the blood, and the three agree as one.

verses.rationale: Preserves the lesser/greater argument and repeated testimony.
verses.before: If we receive human testimony, God's testimony is greater, because this is God's testimony: he has testified concerning his Son.
verses.after: If we accept human testimony, God's testimony is greater. This is God's testimony: he has testified about his Son.
verses.tsw_comparator: If we receive human testimony, the testimony of God is greater, because this is the testimony of God: that God has testified concerning the Son.

verses.rationale: Keeps belief in the Son and belief of God distinct and retains the severe liar claim.
verses.before: The one who trusts in the Son of God has the testimony within. The one who does not trust God has made him a liar, because they have not trusted the testimony God has given concerning his Son.
verses.after: Whoever believes in the Son of God has the testimony within. Whoever does not believe God has made him a liar, because they have not believed the testimony God has given about his Son.
verses.tsw_comparator: The one who trusts in the Son of God has the testimony in themselves. The one who does not trust God has made God a liar, because they have not trusted in the testimony that God has testified concerning the Son.

verses.rationale: Preserves the gift and the location of life in the Son.
verses.before: And this is the testimony: God gave us eternal life, and this life is in his Son.
verses.after: And this is the testimony: God gave us eternal life, and this life is in his Son.
verses.tsw_comparator: And this is the testimony: God gave us eternal life, and this life is in the Son.

verses.rationale: Retains the balanced antithesis and fuller title in the second half.
verses.before: The one who has the Son has life; the one who does not have the Son of God does not have life.
verses.after: Whoever has the Son has life; whoever does not have the Son of God does not have life.
verses.tsw_comparator: The one who has the Son has life; the one who does not have the Son of God does not have life.

verses.rationale: Follows the pinned shorter ending and preserves name and assurance language.
verses.before: I have written these things to you who trust in the name of the Son of God so that you may know that you have eternal life.
verses.after: I have written these things to you who believe in the name of the Son of God so that you may know you have eternal life.
verses.tsw_comparator: I have written these things to you who trust in the name of the Son of God, so that you may know that you have eternal life.

verses.rationale: Keeps the condition according to his will and confidence before him.
verses.before: And this is the confidence we have before him: if we ask anything according to his will, he hears us.
verses.after: This is the confidence we have before him: if we ask anything according to his will, he hears us.
verses.tsw_comparator: And this is the confidence that we have before God: if we ask anything according to God’s will, God hears us.

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated knowing and asking without replacing requests with a new interpretation.
verses.before: And if we know that he hears us in whatever we ask, we know that we have the requests we have asked from him.
verses.after: And if we know that he hears us in whatever we ask, we know that we have the requests we have asked of him.
verses.tsw_comparator: And if we know that God hears us in whatever we ask, we know that we have the requests that we have asked from God.

verses.rationale: Retains the unnamed giver and the distinction between sins without identifying the death-leading sin or turning the last clause into an absolute prohibition.
verses.before: If anyone sees a brother or sister committing a sin not leading to death, they should ask, and God will give life to that person—to those whose sin is not leading to death. There is sin leading to death; I am not saying that one should ask concerning that.
verses.after: If anyone sees a brother or sister committing a sin that does not lead to death, they should ask, and he will give that person life—to those whose sin does not lead to death. There is sin that leads to death; I am not saying they should pray about that.
verses.tsw_comparator: If anyone sees a brother or sister committing a sin not leading to death, they shall ask, and God will give life to that one—to those whose sin is not leading to death. There is sin leading to death; I do not say that one should ask concerning that.

verses.rationale: Keeps both clauses and the recurring unrighteousness term.
verses.before: All unrighteousness is sin, and there is sin not leading to death.
verses.after: All unrighteousness is sin, and there is sin that does not lead to death.
verses.tsw_comparator: All unrighteousness is sin, and there is sin not leading to death.

verses.rationale: Follows the pinned him rather than himself reading and leaves the identity of the protecting one for the note.
verses.before: We know that everyone who has been born of God does not sin, but the one who was born of God keeps them, and the evil one does not touch them.
verses.after: We know that everyone who has been born of God does not sin. But the one who was born of God keeps that person safe, and the evil one does not touch them.
verses.tsw_comparator: We know that everyone who has been born of God does not sin, but the one who was born of God keeps them, and the evil one does not touch them.

verses.rationale: Renders lies in naturally while retaining whole world and the personal evil-one reading.
verses.before: We know that we are from God, and the whole world lies in the power of the evil one.
verses.after: We know that we are of God, and the whole world lies in the power of the evil one.
verses.tsw_comparator: We know that we are from God, and the whole world lies in the power of the evil one.

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated true one and the final this without resolving its debated antecedent.
verses.before: We know that the Son of God has come and has given us understanding so that we may know the True One. And we are in the True One, in his Son Jesus Christ. This one is the true God and eternal life.
verses.after: We know that the Son of God has come and has given us understanding so that we may know the true one. And we are in the true one, in his Son Jesus Christ. This is the true God and eternal life.
verses.tsw_comparator: And we know that the Son of God has come and has given us understanding so that we may know the True One; and we are in the True One, in God’s Son Jesus Christ. This one is the true God and eternal life.

verses.rationale: Preserves the abrupt final warning and omits an Amen absent from the pinned text.
verses.before: Little children, guard yourselves from idols.
verses.after: Little children, guard yourselves from idols.
verses.tsw_comparator: Little children, guard yourselves from idols.
